### Observed differences

- The spacing in event positions between A21 and A32, measured when the ordered pair occurs within five steps, moved toward immediate succession: in the earlier window the pair was most often two positions apart (about 56 in 100), with about 40 in 100 one position apart and about 5 in 100 three positions apart, while in the later window one position apart became the most common (about 58 in 100), two positions fell to about 42 in 100, and three-position lags were no longer observed. [LAG001]
- This profile rests on 88 pair observations in the earlier window and 109 in the later window (out of 200 traces each), so the pair within five steps was also observed somewhat more often later; the spacing difference is larger than in about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data, meaning it is unusual for a random split, but it is reported by a single indicator. [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change in the process. The only qualifying item is one lag-distribution shift for the pair A21–A32, and with 94 units tested about 0.47 items would qualify by chance in an unchanged process, so a single item — however unusual it looks — is what a stable process typically produces. [LAG001]
